files_read: https://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/25181/1/MPRA_paper_25181.pdf (Ropponen 2010, full text via pdftotext; checked fn 3, 8, 15, 16, p. 10 and the 1.58 / 20.8 / 11.5 values)
kill_argument: The strongest remaining case against this question is that H2's label promises more than its test can deliver. H2 says it implements Neumark and Wascher's measurement-error critique. But NW's critique, as the crew's own notes quote it (NW 1995 p. 9), is that the survey's excess variability is spread through the distribution and 'not driven by one or two outliers'. A 5/95 winsorization tests only the tails. A pass would be reported as surviving NW, which their own text rules out. That is a framing defect, fixable in one line, not a flaw in the test. I attacked the rest and it held. H2 is no longer true by construction: Ropponen's CIC average (0.90, about a third of the DiD) shows that distribution-sensitive estimators can shrink the effect below the half-magnitude line. Its sample, closure rule, percentile pool and comparator are now fixed. H1's within-state targets separate rows 3 and 4. The novelty qualifier is narrowed and backed by a logged search. I spot-checked the key Ropponen numbers against the full text, and only the sample behind his 2.72 is misattributed. The question is answerable within budget on public data.

findings.text: H2 was true by construction (a sign test with known positive published answers), and the contribution's pre-specification claim was hollow.
findings.remedy: Narrow the contribution; rewrite H2 with a criterion that can fail and has no published answer.
findings.response: PI: contribution narrowed to no specification search within this study, with the known published checks disclosed; H2 now a winsorization check with no published result found, judged on keeping half the magnitude.
findings.ruling: Resolved in the files. The contribution now says the crew had read the published results of other checks and claims only the absence of within-study search. H2's half-magnitude criterion (about 1.38) can fail: PA's change SD (10.8) exceeds NJ's (8.4, NW 1995 p. 3), so capping tails can shrink the PA decline. Sample and comparator problems in the new H2 are raised separately as F6, and the novelty qualifier as F7.

findings.text: H2's sample and comparator are not fixed, and the open choices can mechanically decide the outcome. (i) A 'store-level change in FTE' exists only for stores observed in both waves. The 'replicated headline estimate' H2 compares against is H1(a), Table 3 row 3, a difference of wave means over all available stores, not a mean of store-level changes. The winsorization effect would then be confounded with a change of sample. (ii) Under CK's closure rule, the six permanently closed stores (5 NJ, 1 PA) have change = minus their wave-1 FTE. These are among the most negative changes in the data, so a pooled 5th-percentile cap raises the NJ mean and pushes H2 toward passing. Whether they are in the winsorized pool is unstated. (iii) Whether the four temporarily closed stores are dropped (row 4) or set to 0 (row 5) is unstated. (iv) Whether the percentiles are computed before or after these exclusions is unstated.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[1] ('store-level changes', 'pooled distribution', 'the replicated headline estimate'); sources/notes.md sec. 1 Table 3 notes (closures) and rows 3-5; sec. 7 item 2
findings.remedy: Fix in plan.json now: the sample is the H1(b) balanced sample (Table 3 row 4: permanent closures = 0, temporary closures missing). Percentiles come from the pooled store-level changes of that sample, closures included. The comparator for 'half the magnitude' is the unwinsorized estimate on that same sample, i.e. replicated row 4, not row 3. Pre-declare as a secondary, reported-not-judged, the same check with the six permanent closures excluded from the winsorization. Each of these is a one-line edit.
findings.response: PI: H2 fixed on the balanced sample with closures as zero, pooled percentiles incl. closures, compared with the unwinsorized estimate on the same sample; secondary excluding closures reported, not judged.
findings.ruling: Resolved in plan.json hypotheses[1]. The sample is the H1(b) balanced sample. Permanent closures are 0 and temporary closures are missing. Percentiles come from the pooled changes of that sample, closures included. The comparator is the unwinsorized estimate on the same sample. The closures-excluded variant is declared secondary and not judged. The percentile interpolation rule (e.g. linear vs nearest-rank, which matters with about 19 stores per pooled tail and about 75 PA stores) is a design detail; I will check it is fixed at the design gate.

findings.text: Obvious prior work is missing, and H2's novelty qualifier rests on a search that is not recorded. The question says winsorization is 'a check with no published result that we found'. But q-novelty was completed before H2 was chosen, and log.jsonl has no search for trimmed, winsorized or distributional reanalyses. Such a search finds Ropponen, 'Minimum Wages and Employment: Replication of Card and Krueger (1994) Using the CIC Estimator' (MPRA Paper 25181, 2010; abstract read), and its journal descendant, Ropponen (2011), 'Reconciling the evidence of Card and Krueger (1994) and Neumark and Wascher (2000)', J. Applied Econometrics 26(6): 1051-1057 (listed on IDEAS, not fetched). The 2010 paper uses the original CK data and Athey-Imbens changes-in-changes, a distribution-level reanalysis. Its abstract concludes that the result 'remains valid only for small fast-food restaurants'. This is a later-literature check on the public data, on the same distributional question H2 asks, and its published result may indicate what winsorization will show. Neither paper is in refs.bib or sources.json. Morshed (2025, OSF preprint 10.31219/osf.io/8ut4n_v1) is another public-data replication not recorded; whether it reproduces the SEs or N = 357 is unchecked, and that bears on the contribution's claim.
findings.evidence: plan.json question ('a check with no published result that we found') and contribution; log.jsonl (no search after 16:39:39Z); sources/notes.md sec. 5-6; refs.bib
findings.remedy: Scout: fetch and verify Ropponen 2011 (JAE) and Ropponen 2010, record them in refs.bib and sources.json, and note in notes.md what they report about the distribution of changes and store size. Skim Morshed 2025 for SEs and N. Log the search terms used for the H2 novelty claim. Then either keep H2 and reword the qualifier to 'no published winsorized estimate; Ropponen (2011) reports a changes-in-changes reanalysis that ...', disclosing what the crew knew, or adopt CIC as the later-literature check. Narrowing the qualifier is the cheaper fix.
findings.response: PI: sent to the Scout to verify Ropponen 2010/2011 and Morshed 2025 and log the search; H2's 'no published result' qualifier removed. Scout: verified and recorded Ropponen 2010 (full text; CIC 0.90 vs DiD 2.72, positive for small and negative for large stores), Ropponen 2011 JAE and 2014 Emp. Econ. (abstracts only; full texts blocked), and Morshed 2025 (full text; does not reproduce 2.76/1.36 or N = 357, reports 3.36); none of the readable sources winsorizes or trims, and NW 1995 p. 9 says the variability is 'not driven by one or two outliers'; search terms logged in sources/notes.md section 5; note that plan.json question still contains 'no published result that we found'.
findings.ruling: Resolved. The question no longer says 'no published result that we found'. It now says 'no published winsorized or trimmed estimate was found' and cites Ropponen's CIC reanalysis alongside. refs.bib and sources.json hold ropponen2010cic (full text), ropponen2011reconciling, ropponen2014note (abstracts) and morshed2025replication (full text). The search terms are logged in notes.md sec. 5. I fetched Ropponen 2010 myself (MPRA 25181) and confirmed: CK balanced sample counted as 309 NJ + 75 PA (fn 8); CIC 0.90 with bootstrap SE 0.44 (fn 16); 8 NJ stores dropped for CIC support (fn 15); 1.58 with controls; lowess zero crossings at 11.5 and 20.8. His fn 3 mentions QDID studies, but those are other minimum-wage studies, not reanalyses of these data. One attribution detail is raised as F12.

findings.text: The seed brief asks for a robustness check 'from the later literature'. H2's winsorization is a crew-built check that no cited work performed. The plan itself calls it a check with no published result, so it sits in tension with the brief. It is defensible only as an operationalization of NW (1995)'s measurement-error critique (SD of changes about three times the payroll data's; extremes of -41.5 and +34 FTE), and plan.json does not say so.
findings.evidence: task.json brief ('pre-specify and report at least one robustness check from the later literature'); plan.json hypotheses[1]; sources/notes.md sec. 2 Finding 1, sec. 7 item 6
findings.remedy: State in H2 that the check operationalizes NW 1995's measurement-error critique, citing neumark1995payroll. Alternatively, also pre-specify the NW sample rule (notes sec. 7 item 6(a); published 2.78) as a second check, reported descriptively and disclosed as having a known published answer.
findings.response: PI: H2 framed as implementing Neumark and Wascher's critique; their sample rule added as a secondary, reported check.
findings.ruling: Resolved as asked. H2 is framed as implementing NW (1995)'s critique, and NW's own sample rule (published 2.78) is a pre-specified secondary check. That rule satisfies the seed brief's 'robustness check from the later literature' on its own. The new framing has its own problem: the Scout found that NW say the excess variability is not driven by outliers. That is raised as F10.

findings.text: H1(a) and H1(b) cannot tell apart the sample rules they are meant to test. Their targets lie within the tolerance of each other: 2.76 vs 2.75, and SE 1.36 vs 1.34. So a single computation on either sample 'reproduces' both, and a wrong sample rule passes. The within-state changes do discriminate, but they are not targeted: NJ 0.59 (0.54) in row 3 vs 0.47 (0.48) in row 4. Two smaller points. 'Within 0.05' is not stated as inclusive, and Mamula's Table 4 estimate of 2.28 sits exactly 0.05 from 2.33. The SE construction is not yet stated (paired within-state SEs combined as independent vs a robust store-level regression), and the crew already knows which one reproduces 1.36.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[0] (a)-(b); sources/notes.md sec. 1 Table 3 rows 3-4 and the SE arithmetic; sec. 5 Mamula (2.28 vs 2.33); sec. 7 item 4
findings.remedy: Add to H1(a)-(b) the within-state change targets: PA -2.16 (1.25), NJ 0.59 (0.54) for row 3, and PA -2.28 (1.25), NJ 0.47 (0.48) for row 4, under the same tolerance. Add store counts per state and wave where the paper reports them. Write the tolerance as |difference| <= 0.05. Fix the SE construction at the design gate, and report the alternative too.
findings.response: PI: within-state targets added; tolerance written as |difference| <= 0.05; SE computation fixed at design.
findings.ruling: Resolved. H1(a)-(b) now carry the within-state targets: PA -2.16 (1.25), NJ 0.59 (0.54) and PA -2.28 (1.25), NJ 0.47 (0.48). These separate the two sample rules (0.59 vs 0.47 is more than 0.05 apart). The tolerance is written as |replicated - published| <= 0.05. The paper gives no per-state store counts, so none can be targeted. The SE construction is deferred to the design gate, as allowed. The crew already knows that the independent-states combination of paired SEs reproduces 1.36, so at design I will require that the alternative (robust store-level regression SE) is reported next to it, as notes.md sec. 7 item 5 proposes.

findings.text: H2 calls itself 'an implementation of Neumark and Wascher's (1995) measurement-error critique'. But the Scout's own reading of NW 1995 (notes.md sec. 5, 'Does any of these report a winsorization...', and sec. 7 item 6; claim c-nw-notoutliers) is that NW state on p. 9 that 'the greater variability in CK's data is not driven by one or two outliers'. NW's critique is that measurement error is diffuse, with a 3x SD ratio across the whole distribution. A 5/95 winsorization tests only the tails. If H2 passes, the label invites the paper to say the estimate 'survives NW's measurement-error critique', a reading NW's own text rules out. notes.md sec. 7 item 6 already says the paper should state this limit, but plan.json does not.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[1] ('an implementation of Neumark and Wascher's (1995) measurement-error critique'); sources/notes.md sec. 5 (NW p. 9 quote) and sec. 7 item 6; claims.jsonl c-nw-notoutliers
findings.remedy: Reword H2's label to 'a tail-only check motivated by Neumark and Wascher's (1995) documentation of extreme survey changes (-41.5, +34 FTE). NW state the excess variability is not outlier-driven, so a pass does not answer their broader measurement-error critique.' A one-line edit; no change to the test.

findings.text: The question asks 'how much of the headline estimate remains' after winsorization. 'Headline' is the Table 3 row 3 estimate (2.76; c-pub-did). But H2, correctly after F6, compares against the unwinsorized balanced-sample estimate (row 4, 2.75). The two numbers are close, so the gap is wording, not substance. Still, the question and the hypothesis name different comparators, and a writer following the question could set the winsorized number against row 3.
findings.evidence: plan.json question ('how much of the headline estimate remains') vs hypotheses[1] ('the unwinsorized difference on the same sample')
findings.remedy: Change 'the headline estimate' in the question to 'the balanced-sample estimate'.

findings.text: The source does not clearly support the sample attributed to Ropponen's DiD of 2.72. Claim c-ropponen-cic says the CIC 0.90 is set 'against a difference-in-differences of 2.72 on the same balanced sample'. notes.md sec. 5 says 'the DiD on this sample [the 384-store balanced sample] is 2.72', and sec. 6 counts Ropponen as reproducing 2.72 'on the balanced sample'. In the paper (MPRA 25181, p. 10), 2.72 is the DiD line in Figure 3. Footnote 15 says that figure uses 301 NJ + 75 PA stores, the CIC support sample with 8 NJ stores dropped. Ropponen only says 2.72 'corresponds to' CK's 2.75. So 2.72 may be on 376 stores, not 384. That matters, because sec. 7 item 2 offers Ropponen's 384 count as a cross-check for H1(b), and sec. 6 lists him as a near-replication of the balanced estimate.
findings.evidence: claims.jsonl c-ropponen-cic; sources/notes.md sec. 5 Ropponen bullet 'Replication', sec. 6 H1 bullet; Ropponen 2010 p. 10 and fn 15 (fetched by the Reviewer)
findings.remedy: Scout: reword to 'a DiD of 2.72, which he says corresponds to CK's 2.75; the figure reporting it uses 301 NJ and 75 PA stores'. Do not call it a replication on the 384-store sample unless the text says so.
